> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 60b99f8fdb96b6d2dcd24af7d23486e4b55e4d66` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `454eae2abd1b89ff97768edd790a3743cd196499` — the merge of head `c62a693463ff34a87bdf4074c6c7c200751a1b5d` into base `60b99f8fdb96b6d2dcd24af7d23486e4b55e4d66`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 454eae2abd1b89ff97768edd790a3743cd196499 && git checkout 454eae2abd1b89ff97768edd790a3743cd196499
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 60b99f8fdb96b6d2dcd24af7d23486e4b55e4d66 c62a693463ff34a87bdf4074c6c7c200751a1b5d && git checkout -B drift-repro 60b99f8fdb96b6d2dcd24af7d23486e4b55e4d66 && git merge --no-ff c62a693463ff34a87bdf4074c6c7c200751a1b5d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 60b99f8fdb96b6d2dcd24af7d23486e4b55e4d66
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 60b99f8fdb96b6d2dcd24af7d23486e4b55e4d66` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · reviewed at `29afc6e5`, merged with `origin/main` to `5eb1c913` by the seat (K was 34) · 2026-11-10T16:41Z · card #32174

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #32174`. Files: `packages/core/src/utils/metadata-activation-store.ts` +116/−12 with its test, a new runtime door test, and a service-automation ledger test, plus the changeset. All are inside the claimed surface, and `activation-ledger-backfill.ts` is untouched (#32096 in flight).
- **Fix, read in the diff:** `setActive` now goes through `addressedLedgerRow`. The rows a write can mean are the package-less ones plus the write's own package's row (the backfill's `duplicated` set, via one shared `namesNoPackage`). More than one candidate is refused with `{code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', status: 409}`, naming every row and the remedy, and nothing is written. That is the existing ADR-0150 two-holder pair, so no new code and `Clause-②: no` stands. The doors are unchanged: the dev measured that each relays the declared pair.
- **Wider than the card, accepted:** with no row the write could mean, two or more rows of other packages are refused too (pinned), and a write beside another package's row now takes its own or the package-less row where storage order used to pick.
- **Tests read:** store refusals assert `code` + `status`, both ids, and zero writes; there are controls; the real `toggleFlow` relays the envelope; and the new runtime test drives all three mounted doors over a real SQLite ledger both ways (409 with the ledger unchanged; one row deleted → 200). The ablation was recorded faithfully after one discarded non-faithful attempt: core rebuilt, marker proven in dist, red 5/1/3, then restored with `--absent` preflight and green again.
- **Gates:** the dev ran 69 derived families, 69 exit 0, and `pnpm lint` exit 0. CI is re-running on `5eb1c913` after the main merge, and landing waits for it.
- **Acceptance notes (noted, not filed: reach not measured):** (1) `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts` `setActivation` flips the first `(metadata_type, name)` row's `active`, the same storage-order family, read and not reproduced. (2) With no own or package-less row, a write still re-addresses another package's one row to its own package. That is unchanged by this PR and only reachable once a type's readers key the ledger by `(package, name)` (its ADR-0150 child).
- **Landing:** non-governed (552 lines ≤ 3000); ready + auto-merge once CI on `5eb1c913` is green.

## 席位核对 · conflict round

**ACCEPT** · head `c62a6934` · 2026-11-10T18:48Z · card #32174 (supersedes record 6773242094 for this head)

- **Why the round:** the merge queue ejected `5eb1c913` with MERGE_CONFLICT against #32239 (`c62e72a4`, flows held, armed and run by `(package, name)`). Both changed `setActive` in `packages/core/src/utils/metadata-activation-store.ts`.
- **Resolution, read in the diff:** one merge commit (`8d19f88e`), with no rebase and no force-push. `addressedLedgerRow` now reads the store's addressing. By name (actions, catalog), the behaviour is unchanged from the accepted head. By package and name (flows), #32239's addressing holds: the package's own row, or the package-less rows it adopts when it holds the name alone. Two or more candidates are refused with the same 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, naming every row. That refusal also closes this card's defect on #32239's adopt path (it took the first of two package-less rows), reproduced on the merged code with the guard ablated.
- **The seat's acceptance note 2, re-judged on the merged code:** two packages' same-named flows can now each hold a row, and a write for B never rewrites A's only row. In flow mode A's row is never a candidate, so B gets its own row. Pinned in core and through the real `toggleFlow` (insert B's own row, update it next switch, A's row unchanged). The by-name re-address of an item's one other-package row stays only for types whose readers still read by name (ADR-0150 red line 3; #32239's own pin), where no writer puts two packages' rows of one name. Note 2 is closed.
- **Tests and ablation:** core 55/55, service-automation 51/51, runtime 3/3. The guard was ablated on `c62a6934` (marker proven in dist, then removed with `--absent`): red 6 / 1 / 3 and green again after restore. 69 derived gate families exit 0. CI on `c62a6934`: 55 success · 11 skipped · 0 failed.
- **PR body:** the seat added the flow-mode paragraph to "What changes", from the dev's addendum 6776121913. The changeset already carries it.
- **Landing:** non-governed; ready + auto-merge once the body checks re-run green and K is re-read.
